status: Resolved user-confirmed design and candidate contracts; native application unimplemented
decision: Each feature owns one active approved plan and at most one pending revision. Keep the original plan open and approved until replacement approval; no separate plan lifecycle or user-facing version management.
behavior: Saving/requesting approval/rejecting a revision preserves active approval and eligible work.
Pending scope cannot authorize implementation or live task acceptance changes.
Exact authenticated approval atomically replaces active plan/scope/acceptance/history and clears the pending slot.
Changed draft makes an approval stale; unrelated metadata need not invalidate an unchanged draft.
Existing manual holds remain; only incompatible work is fenced when approved changes are adopted at safe boundaries.
storage: One feature_plans row holds active and pending content; existing feature history provides audit. The plan_revisions catalog is removed from the design fixture. Existing revision/digest fields remain internal concurrency and approval binding tokens.
sqliteChecks: saving pending content preserves the approved plan
reopen retains approved and pending content separately
requesting approval does not invalidate the original approval
stale draft approval cannot replace the current plan
interrupted promotion rolls back plan, approval and event together
approval atomically replaces the plan and clears the one pending slot
plan approval does not clear a manual pause
feature owns one plan-state row rather than a plan-version catalog
limits: The SQLite checks exercise fixture transactions and rollback, not production human authority or application services.
Prototype decisions are simulated local sample state, not native execution or authorization.
DW-009/012/014/015 must implement and qualify actual admission, root/task adoption, source evidence and recovery.
